context.title: Glory, Faith and Greatness
context.summary: Jesus is transfigured before three disciples. Below the mountain he heals a boy the others could not help, predicts his death again, and teaches that the greatest is the servant of all.
context.background: Mark does not name the mountain; Tabor and Hermon are traditional guesses. Moses and Elijah represent the Law and the Prophets. 'Hell' in vv. 43–47 translates Gehenna, the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, once a site of child sacrifice (Jeremiah 7:31) and later an image of final judgment.

customs.note: The law required salt on grain offerings (Leviticus 2:13). Salt preserved and purified; Jesus' saying links it with testing that refines his followers.

watchFor: The father's honest cry: 'Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief' (v. 24).
The disciples argue about greatness right after Jesus speaks of his death (vv. 31–34).
Jesus takes a child in his arms as an object lesson (v. 36).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: John
people.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Capernaum
places.summary: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth (Matt. 4:13-16; Luke 4:16-31), Capernaum became his “own city.”
